tone_statements.quote: Tonecat: None. Tone: The language appears to be non-tonal. [...] Stresscat: Minor. Stress: Based on remarks by Morgan (1996: 19-20), quoting observations by Gueye (1980), stress appears to be non-functional, and sometimes even hard to determine. It normally appears to fall on the first syllable, but "when a two syllable word ends with an open syllable, or has a long vowel in other than the first syllable, it is difficult to determine the place of stress. Both syllables seem to receive equal stress."

sources.citation: Zuk, Fabian. 2024. Review of Merrill, John T. M., The Cangin languages. Linguistique et langues africaines 10(2). doi:10.4000/13lt8
sources.note: Review summarises the book's phonology chapter as consonant/vowel reconstruction, phonotactics and sound change; says nothing about stress, accent or prosody.

sources.citation: Mbengue, Massaer & Daniel Morgan. 2021. Manuel pour lire et écrire le ndút, 5ème édition (1ère éd. 2000 = Glottolog ref 82400). Dakar: SIL Sénégal. 99 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on word stress. Introductory notes cover dialect variants (Palu, Gíjëer), glottalised and prenasalised consonants and vowel length; 'accent' appears only as the orthographic mark on é/í/ú for vowel quality (pp. 1119, 1370, 1653 of text dump).

sources.note: SECONDHAND (compiler's summary of Morgan 1996 / Gueye 1986, not a first-hand description): tone category 'None', note 'The language appears to be non-tonal.' NB the same compiler's WALS feature 13A codes Ndut as 'Complex tone system' on Gueye 1986 - the two Maddieson databases contradict each other; the LAPSyD prose note is the deliberate one and the WALS value looks like a coding slip, but only Gueye 1986 / Morgan 1996: 19-20 / Gueye 1980 can settle it.

sources.note: SECONDHAND database code: 13A = 'Complex tone system' attributed to Gueye, G. 1986, 'Les correlats articulatoires et acoustiques de la distinction +/- ATR en Ndut', Travaux de l'Institut de Phonétique de Strasbourg 18: 137-249. Contradicted by the same author's LAPSyD entry (Tone: None, 'appears to be non-tonal') built from the same sources; treat as a pointer/flag, not as evidence - the primary sources to check are Gueye 1986 and Morgan 1996: 19-20 (both already listed here, unread).
